about.title: South Pasadena Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: South Pasadena residents rely on nearby Los Angeles County hospitals and clinics for everything from routine care to emergency treatment, and most of the time that care goes fine. But when a surgical error, a missed diagnosis, or a medication mistake causes real harm, families are often left confused about whether what happened crosses the line into malpractice. California law sets a narrow window to act and requires a qualified medical expert to weigh in before a claim can move forward, which makes early attorney involvement important. LawProactive doesn't practice law or evaluate your medical records ourselves — we simply connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney in our network who can review what happened, explain your options, and take the case on contingency if it moves forward. A hospital stay that ends badly isn't automatically malpractice, but you deserve a clear answer either way.

whyChoose.title: What to Know Before You Act

items.title: The Clock Starts Early
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discover the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself, to bring a claim. Waiting to sort out what happened can quietly cost you your case.

items.title: 90-Day Notice Comes First
items.desc: Before a malpractice lawsuit can be filed, California law requires a 90-day written notice to the provider. Missing this step, or getting the timing wrong, can delay or derail a valid claim.

items.title: Non-Economic Damages Are Capped, Not Eliminated
items.desc: MICRA places a cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, though that cap rises each year. An attorney can walk through what categories of loss may apply to your situation.

items.question: I had a bad outcome after surgery — does that automatically mean malpractice happened?
items.answer: No. California law recognizes that medicine carries risk, and a poor result by itself isn't proof of negligence. A malpractice claim generally requires showing the provider deviated from the accepted standard of care, which is why a qualified medical expert almost always has to review the case first.

items.question: Where would I even get treated for something that happened in South Pasadena?
items.answer: Most South Pasadena residents are treated at Los Angeles County-area hospitals and clinics rather than a local hospital in the city itself, since South Pasadena is a small community. An attorney connected through LawProactive can help identify which facility's records and providers are relevant to your claim.

items.question: What does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney in our network, and attorneys who take malpractice cases typically work on contingency, meaning they're only paid if you recover money. There's no obligation to move forward after that first conversation.
